docs.title: AsyncArenasPlus: Minecraft Area and Arena Reset Plugin
docs.text:
AsyncArenasPlus is a Minecraft Java server plugin for restoring selected areas and arenas to saved states. Use it to reset PvP arenas, repair spawn areas, restore minigame maps, or rotate one region between different terrain layouts. Resets can run manually or automatically on a timer.

Normal arena creation and resets do not require WorldEdit, FastAsyncWorldEdit (FAWE), or another plugin.

Get AsyncArenasPlus on BuiltByBit Installation and setup

docs.title: Reset a Minecraft arena every five minutes
docs.text:
After installing and activating the plugin:

  1. Run /arena wand and select two opposite corners of the area you want to restore.
  2. Run /arena create pvp to save the arena's current state.
  3. Change a few blocks inside the area, then run /arena reset pvp to verify that they return to the saved state.
  4. Run /arena periodic pvp 5m to reset the arena automatically every five minutes.

The selection is the region that will be restored, so check its boundaries before enabling automatic resets. See the full setup guide for coordinates, time formats, and terrain rotation.

docs.title: What can you reset?
docs.text:
Server area Example workflow PvP, Crystal PvP, or practice arena Save the arena before play and restore it manually or on a timer. Spawn or public building area Periodically return the selected region to its saved layout. Mine or minigame map Restore the blocks captured in the saved arena. Arena with multiple terrain layouts Save variants of the same region and rotate between them.

A reset restores a saved region. It does not generate a new world or automatically provide minigame rules, queues, or match-end detection.

docs.title: Compatibility and dependencies
docs.text: Requirement Details Edition and server software Minecraft Java Edition; Paper and Folia. Check the current product listing for the Minecraft versions supported by the build you purchase. WorldEdit or FAWE Not required for normal arena creation and resets. An optional compatibility layer supports external editing workflows. PlaceholderAPI Optional; adds reset countdown placeholders. An existing arena plugin Only required while importing arenas from that plugin. License setup Follow the installation instructions to activate a purchased build.

docs.title: AsyncArenas or AsyncArenasPlus?
docs.text:
AsyncArenas and AsyncArenasPlus are separate paid plugins by the same creator. AsyncArenas uses a FAWE-based workflow. Plus has its own reset workflow and does not require FAWE for normal resets.

Plus is designed for repeated arena restoration while players are online, with controls for pacing player-visible updates. Actual reset duration and smoothness depend on the arena, server, settings, and nearby players; there is no universal zero-lag guarantee.

Read the arena reset plugin comparison for tradeoffs, free alternatives, and how to evaluate reset performance on your server. Existing AsyncArenas users can migrate saved arenas.

docs.title: Can I automatically reset a selected Minecraft area?
docs.text: Yes. Select two corners, save the region with /arena create <name>, and set a timer with /arena periodic <name> <time>. For example, /arena periodic pvp 5m resets the saved pvp arena every five minutes.

docs.title: Does an arena reset restore my build or regenerate the world seed?
docs.text: It restores the region to the state saved when you created or last edited that arena. To change the saved layout, follow the template editing workflow.

docs.title: Can I display a countdown before the next reset?
docs.text: Yes. With PlaceholderAPI installed, use %asyncarenasplus_reset_time_pvp% for an arena named pvp. See countdown placeholders for additional formats and multiple arenas.

docs.title: Where are the commands and troubleshooting steps?
docs.text: See arena commands, configuration, and troubleshooting. For support, use the AsyncArenasPlus Discord.

docs.title: Minecraft Arena Reset Plugins: AsyncArenas and AsyncArenasPlus Compared
docs.text:
A Minecraft arena reset plugin restores a selected region to a saved state. The right choice depends on whether you need a manual restore, automatic area resets, terrain rotation, or repeated resets while players are watching. Compare the workflow and dependencies as well as performance on your own server.

This guide is maintained by the AsyncArenasPlus project. It explains where our plugins fit alongside general world editors and free alternatives.

docs.title: Which reset approach fits your server?
docs.text:
Approach Useful for Dependencies and tradeoffs AsyncArenas A paid arena reset plugin with a FAWE-based workflow. Check its own listing for dependencies, supported versions, and compatibility notices. Plus is a separate plugin. AsyncArenasPlus Scheduled or manual saved-region resets, terrain rotation, reset countdowns, and migration from supported plugins. Paid; no WorldEdit or FAWE required for normal resets. Includes controls for pacing player-visible updates. WorldEdit or FastAsyncWorldEdit General world editing and restoring schematics as part of an administrator's workflow. A recurring reset workflow may need additional commands, scheduling, or integration. Compare the exact paste settings you use. Free dedicated tools such as AreaReset or Blossom An alternative to evaluate for straightforward area restoration. Verify each project's current maintenance, version support, dependencies, and scheduling features before choosing it.

A free tool that meets your requirements can be a good choice. There is no need to replace a working setup solely because another plugin advertises faster resets.

docs.title: How do AsyncArenas and AsyncArenasPlus differ?
docs.text:
AsyncArenas uses a FAWE-based reset workflow. AsyncArenasPlus uses its own arena restoration workflow, with manual resets, periodic resets, terrain rotations, and optional PlaceholderAPI countdowns. Normal Plus arena creation and resets do not require FAWE or WorldEdit.

Plus is intended for operators who want those features together with control over visible update delivery during repeated live resets. It can import arenas from AsyncArenas, AreaResetterPro, and AreaReloader-FAWE. Check both product listings before purchasing: support for a server version or integration in one plugin does not imply support in the other.

docs.title: How do I automatically reset a Minecraft area?
docs.text:
With AsyncArenasPlus installed and activated:

  1. Run /arena wand and select two corners.
  2. Run /arena create pvp to save the region.
  3. Change some blocks and run /arena reset pvp to test restoration.
  4. Run /arena periodic pvp 5m to repeat the reset every five minutes.

See installation and automatic reset setup for the full workflow. This restores the saved layout; it does not generate new terrain from the world seed.

docs.title: Why can players notice lag during a reset?
docs.text:
Restoring blocks and showing those changes to players are related costs. A reset may finish its server-side work quickly while clients are still receiving or rendering updates. Arena size, changed blocks, nearby viewers, hardware, network capacity, and reset settings can all affect the result.

AsyncArenasPlus is designed to avoid unnecessary updates and pace visible updates using its update queue. Higher queue limits can make changes appear sooner but can also increase bursts. Lower limits can spread updates over a longer period. See update queue configuration and troubleshooting slow visual updates.

WorldEdit and FAWE are general world editors with configurable behavior. Performance comparisons should identify the exact versions and settings rather than assume every schematic workflow behaves the same way.

docs.title: How should I compare arena reset performance?
docs.text:
For a more thorough comparison than general statements, see the Minecraft arena/area reset plugin benchmark. It describes the test scenarios and methodology, reports CPU usage, network traffic, heap allocation, peak network rate, and worst tick measurements, and provides the result tables as JSON. The results apply to the tested configurations and workloads.

Test the same saved region, damage pattern, and nearby-player count with each plugin. Record:

  • Server hardware, Minecraft build, Java version, plugin versions, and reset settings.
  • Arena dimensions, the amount of damage, and how many players can see the reset.
  • Server-side completion time, MSPT during the reset, and outgoing network traffic.
  • How long players take to see the restored arena and whether updates arrive smoothly.
  • Results from repeated runs, including a quiet server and your expected busy-server conditions.

Test on a copy or a non-production arena first. This guide does not establish a measured speed multiplier or promise zero lag for every server.

docs.title: Can I rotate between different arena maps?
docs.text:
Yes. Save multiple terrain variants with the same region bounds, then run:

/arena rotation 5m arena_variant_a arena_variant_b arena_variant_c

This rotates the shared area between the saved variants every five minutes. Follow the terrain rotation instructions when creating the variants.

docs.title: Is this a full minigame or whole-world reset system?
docs.text:
AsyncArenasPlus restores saved areas. Match rules, player queues, and deciding when a duel has ended belong to your minigame workflow. A complete world wipe or new world generation is also a different task.

Explore AsyncArenasPlus features or get the plugin on BuiltByBit.

docs.title: Arena Commands
docs.text:
All normal arena commands are under:

/arena

Required permission:

asyncarenasplus.admin

docs.title: Time values
docs.text:
Commands that accept time use the same parser:

  • 10s: seconds
  • 5m: minutes
  • 3h: hours
  • 1d: days
  • 20t: ticks

Use an explicit unit in commands. No-suffix values are treated as ticks.

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
Create from your current wand selection:

/arena create <name> [time]

Create from exact coordinates:

/arena create <name> <world> <x1> <y1> <z1> <x2> <y2> <z2> [time]

If a time is provided, it becomes the arena's periodic reset interval.

docs.title: Wand
docs.text:
/arena wand

Gives the arena selection amethyst shard to an in-game player.

Selection controls:

  • Left click: position 1
  • Right click: position 2

docs.title: Reset
docs.text:
/arena reset <name>

Runs a manual arena reset.

docs.title: Edit
docs.text:
/arena edit <name>

Saves the arena from the current world state while keeping the same bounds and schedule.

Recommended workflow:

/arena pause <time>
/arena reset <name>

Make your changes, then run:

/arena edit <name>
/arena pause off

docs.title: Info
docs.text:
/arena info <name>

Shows:

  • display name
  • world
  • bounds
  • clickable midpoint teleport
  • automatic reset schedule and next reset time

docs.title: List
docs.text:
/arena list

Shows all loaded arenas with display name, world, and periodic reset schedule.

docs.title: Display Name
docs.text:
/arena displayname <arena> <new display name>

Sets the public display name stored in config.yml under arena-display-names.

Arena files use the name you entered when creating the arena. Display names let placeholders and command output show a cleaner public name without renaming the arena file.

Example:

/arena displayname pvp_1 PVP Arena 1

docs.title: Periodic Reset Schedule
docs.text:
/arena periodic <name> <time> [offset]

Behavior:

  • time sets the interval.
  • offset is optional and delays when that arena starts its schedule.
  • You do not need to specify an offset.
  • A time of 0 disables automatic resets for that arena.

Examples:

/arena periodic mine_1 15m
/arena periodic mine_1 15m 2m
/arena periodic mine_1 0

docs.title: Rotation Setup
docs.text:
/arena rotation <time_between_resets> <arena1> <arena2> [arena3...]

This configures all listed arenas as one rotation.

Example:

/arena rotation 5m red blue green

This rotates the shared gameplay area between red, blue, and green, with one variant applying every 5 minutes.

docs.title: Pause Or Resume Automatic Resets
docs.text:
Pause all automatic periodic resets:

/arena pause <time>

Resume:

/arena pause off

resume is also accepted:

/arena pause resume

Check status:

/arena pause status

/arena pause 0 also resumes automatic resets.

docs.title: Reload Configuration
docs.text:
/arena reload

Reloads config.yml, display names, and configured periodic schedules.

docs.title: Delete Arena
docs.text:
/arena delete <name>

Deletes the arena from memory and removes its .aarena file if it exists.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
Use the default available provider:

/arena migrate <name|all>

Use a specific provider:

/arena migrate <provider> <name|all>

Providers:

  • asyncarenas
  • arearesetterpro
  • areareloader-fawe

See Migration Guide for behavior and naming rules.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The main config file is:

plugins/AsyncArenasPlus/config.yml

Run this after editing it:

/arena reload

docs.title: Loader License
docs.text:
If you bought AsyncArenasPlus, start the server once after installing the plugin jar. The plugin creates:

plugins/AsyncArenasPlus/loader.yml

Put the license from the purchase Discord into loader.yml, then restart the server.

docs.title: Periodic Resets
docs.text:
periodic-resets: {}
periodic-offsets: {}
periodic-resets Controls how often each arena resets automatically. The key is the arena name and the value is the reset interval. periodic-offsets Optional. Delays when an arena starts its reset schedule. This is useful when you have multiple arenas and do not want all of them resetting at the same time.

Example:

periodic-resets:
  mine_1: 15m
  mine_2: 15m
periodic-offsets:
  mine_2: 5m

In this example, both arenas reset every 15 minutes, but mine_2 starts 5 minutes later than mine_1.

Most arenas do not need an offset.

Time values support 10s, 5m, 3h, 1d, 20t, or a raw tick value with no suffix. Use explicit units in normal configs.

docs.title: Display Names
docs.text:
arena-display-names: {}

Arena files use the name from /arena create <name>. Display names let command output and placeholders show a cleaner public name without renaming the arena file.

Example:

arena-display-names:
  mine_1: Mine Arena 1

docs.title: Reset Packets
docs.text:
reset-packets:
  use-precise-dirty-blocks: false
  send-light-updates: true
use-precise-dirty-blocks Advanced/debug option for reset packet behavior. Do not change this unless you know what you are doing or have been asked to while troubleshooting. send-light-updates Sends lighting updates to players after arena resets. Keep this enabled if players need lighting to update immediately after a reset.

docs.title: Reset Section Preparation
docs.text:
reset-sections:
  preparation-mode: construct-from-scratch

Supported values:

  • construct-from-scratch: safest option and the recommended default.
  • copy: can be faster, but can cause weird issues in certain server/plugin contexts.

Stick to construct-from-scratch unless you have tested your server, confirmed this part is actually too slow, and verified that copy behaves correctly in your setup.

docs.title: Update Queue
docs.text:
update-queue:
  enabled: true
  max-sections-per-player-per-tick: 6
  max-queued-sections-per-player: 10000
enabled Controls whether visible reset updates are smoothed out for players instead of being sent all at once. max-sections-per-player-per-tick Controls how quickly each player receives visible reset updates. Higher values make reset visuals appear faster, but send more packets at once. max-queued-sections-per-player Limits how many visible reset updates can wait for one player. This prevents unbounded queues during very large resets.

docs.title: Arena Files
docs.text:
AsyncArenasPlus stores arena files in:

plugins/AsyncArenasPlus/arenas/

Each arena is stored as:

<arenaName>.aarena

docs.title: How to Set Up Automatic Minecraft Arena Resets
docs.text: This guide creates a saved Minecraft arena and restores it on a timer with AsyncArenasPlus. WorldEdit and FAWE are not required. Check the current product listing for supported Minecraft versions before installing a build.

docs.title: Example: reset an area every five minutes
docs.text:
After completing the installation and license setup below, run /arena wand and select two corners of your arena. Save it with /arena create pvp, change a few blocks, and test /arena reset pvp. Then run /arena periodic pvp 5m to enable automatic resets every five minutes.

You need the asyncarenasplus.admin permission; server operators have it by default. Verify the selected boundaries and saved layout before enabling a timer.

docs.title: 1. Install plugins
docs.text:
Required:

  • AsyncArenasPlus

No other plugin is required for normal arena creation and resets.

docs.title: 2. License loader setup
docs.text:
If you bought AsyncArenasPlus:

  1. Put the plugin jar in your server's plugins folder.
  2. Start the server once.
  3. Stop the server.
  4. Open:
plugins/AsyncArenasPlus/loader.yml
  1. Add the license from the purchase Discord.
  2. Start the server again.

Optional:

  • PlaceholderAPI, if you want reset countdown placeholders.
  • AsyncArenas, AreaResetterPro, or AreaReloader-FAWE, if you want to migrate existing arenas.

docs.title: 3. Create your first arena
docs.text:
1. Get the arena selection item:
/arena wand

  1. Use the amethyst shard to select two corners of your arena area.

  2. Create the arena:

/arena create <name>

Optional: create and set periodic reset in one step:

/arena create <name> <time>

Tip: you can also create by coordinates:

/arena create <name> <world> <x1> <y1> <z1> <x2> <y2> <z2> [time]

Time values support 10s, 5m, 3h, 1d, 20t, or a raw tick value with no suffix.

docs.title: 4. Verify reset
docs.text:
1. Change blocks inside the arena.
  2. Run:
/arena reset <name>

docs.title: 5. Set periodic resets
docs.text:
Basic:

/arena periodic <name> <time>

Offset is optional. Most arenas do not need one.

Optional offset example:

/arena periodic <name> <time> <offset>

Example:

/arena periodic pvp_1 15m 2m

This means:

  • pvp_1 resets every 15 minutes
  • it waits 2 minutes before starting that schedule, which can help spread resets out

Use /arena pause <time> to temporarily stop all automatic periodic resets, /arena pause off to resume, and /arena pause status to check the current state.

docs.title: 6. Rotate one gameplay area between multiple terrain variants
docs.text:
If you want one physical area to cycle through different terrain versions:

  1. Create arena variant A for that area.
  2. Change the area to variant B and create a second arena with the same bounds.
  3. Run the rotation command.

Example:

/arena rotation 5m arena_variant_a arena_variant_b

This makes the same area alternate between stored variants every 5 minutes.

docs.title: 7. Inspect the result
docs.text:
Useful checks after setup:

/arena list
/arena info <name>

/arena info <name> shows bounds, display name, and next periodic reset timing.

docs.title: AsyncArenasPlus Arena Reset Features
docs.text: AsyncArenasPlus combines saved-region restoration, automatic reset timers, terrain rotation, and optional countdown placeholders. Use the examples below after installing the plugin.

docs.title: Arena creation
docs.text:
Use /arena wand, click two corners, then run /arena create <name>.

This is the normal workflow for creating new arenas.

Console users, command blocks, and scripted setup can create arenas with exact coordinates:

/arena create <name> <world> <x1> <y1> <z1> <x2> <y2> <z2> [time]

docs.title: Manual arena resets
docs.text:
Use:

/arena reset <name>

for immediate resets during events, testing, or moderation.

docs.title: Editing saved templates
docs.text:
To update the saved version of an arena:

  1. Pause automatic resets.
  2. Reset the arena you want to modify.
  3. Make your changes in the world.
  4. Save the new version.

Commands:

/arena pause <time>
/arena reset <name>
/arena edit <name>

After you are done, resume automatic resets:

/arena pause off

docs.title: Periodic resets
docs.text:
Use:

/arena periodic <name> <time> [offset]

How it behaves:

  • time: how often the arena resets
  • offset: optional delay before that arena starts its schedule
  • You do not need to specify an offset.

You can globally pause/resume automatic periodic resets with:

/arena pause <time|off|status>

Time values support 10s, 5m, 3h, 1d, 20t, or a raw tick value with no suffix.

docs.title: Terrain rotation
docs.text:
Use rotation when one gameplay area should cycle through multiple terrain variants.

Typical setup:

  1. Create multiple arenas that cover the same area, each saved in a different terrain state.
  2. Run the rotation command.
/arena rotation <time_between_resets> <arena1> <arena2> [arena3...]

Example:

/arena rotation 5m red blue green

This rotates the shared gameplay area between red, blue, and green, with one variant applying every 5 minutes.

docs.title: Display names
docs.text:
Arena files use the name you entered when creating the arena. If that name is not clean enough for public placeholders or command output, set a display name:

/arena displayname <arena> <new display name>

Display names are shown by /arena list, /arena info, and PlaceholderAPI placeholders that return arena names.

docs.title: PlaceholderAPI reset countdowns
docs.text:
When PlaceholderAPI is installed, AsyncArenasPlus registers the asyncarenasplus expansion.

Supported placeholders:

  • %asyncarenasplus_reset_time_<arena>%
  • %asyncarenasplus_reset_soonest_time_<arena1,arena2,...>%
  • %asyncarenasplus_reset_soonest_name_<arena1,arena2,...>%

See PlaceholderAPI for examples and return values.

docs.title: Low-lag resets and compatibility
docs.text:
AsyncArenasPlus is designed for repeated arena resets during normal gameplay, with a configurable queue for pacing player-visible updates. Actual reset time and smoothness depend on arena size, server resources, nearby players, and configuration. See reset performance and comparison.

An optional WorldEdit compatibility layer is available for servers that use external editing workflows.

docs.title: Migration from other arena plugins
docs.text:
You can import existing arenas from supported providers using /arena migrate ....

Current providers:

  • asyncarenas
  • arearesetterpro
  • areareloader-fawe

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: AsyncArenasPlus can import arenas from supported plugins.

docs.title: Supported Sources
docs.text:
• asyncarenas
  • arearesetterpro
  • areareloader-fawe

docs.title: Requirement
docs.text:
The plugin you are migrating from must be installed, enabled, and running on the server while you migrate.

After the migration is complete and you have confirmed the arenas work in AsyncArenasPlus, you can disable or remove the old plugin.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Migrate using the first available source plugin:

/arena migrate <name|all>

Migrate from a specific source plugin:

/arena migrate <provider> <name|all>

Examples:

/arena migrate all
/arena migrate asyncarenas all
/arena migrate arearesetterpro mine_1

docs.title: After Migration
docs.text:
Check the imported arenas:

/arena list
/arena info <arena>
/arena reset <arena>

If you want a nicer public name, set one with:

/arena displayname <arena> <new display name>

docs.title: PlaceholderAPI
docs.text:
AsyncArenasPlus registers PlaceholderAPI placeholders only when PlaceholderAPI is installed and enabled.

Identifier:

asyncarenasplus

docs.title: Single Arena Reset Time
docs.text:
%asyncarenasplus_reset_time_<arena>%

Returns the time until the arena's next periodic reset.

Examples:

%asyncarenasplus_reset_time_mine_1%
%asyncarenasplus_reset_time_pvp_1%

Return values:

  • now: reset time is due or overdue
  • never: arena does not exist or has no next periodic reset scheduled
  • a compact duration such as 45s, 5m, 1h 20m, or 2d 3h 10m

docs.title: Soonest Reset Time
docs.text:
%asyncarenasplus_reset_soonest_time_<arena1,arena2,...>%

Returns the shortest reset countdown from a comma-separated arena list.

Example:

%asyncarenasplus_reset_soonest_time_mine_1,mine_2,mine_3%

Return values:

  • never: no listed arena has a scheduled next reset
  • a compact duration such as 20s, 4m, or 1h 5m

docs.title: Soonest Reset Name
docs.text:
%asyncarenasplus_reset_soonest_name_<arena1,arena2,...>%

Returns the display name of the listed arena with the soonest scheduled reset.

Example:

%asyncarenasplus_reset_soonest_name_mine_1,mine_2,mine_3%

Return values:

  • none: no listed arena has a scheduled next reset
  • the arena display name, if configured
  • otherwise the arena's internal name

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Arena names are comma-separated with no special escaping.
  • Blank arena names in a list are ignored.
  • Display names are configured with /arena displayname <arena> <new display name>.
  • Placeholders use scheduled periodic reset times; manual resets do not create a future scheduled reset by themselves.

docs.title: Arena is not resetting as expected
docs.text:
1. Confirm the arena exists:
/arena list
  1. Check the arena details:
/arena info <name>
  1. Run a manual reset:
/arena reset <name>

If the saved arena version is wrong, update it with the safe edit workflow:

/arena pause <time>
/arena reset <name>

Make your changes, then save them:

/arena edit <name>
/arena pause off

docs.title: Players see resets slowly
docs.text:
Large arenas may need more time to visually update for every player.

If you know what you are doing, you can adjust:

update-queue:
  enabled: true
  max-sections-per-player-per-tick: 6

Higher values make reset visuals appear faster but can increase packet bursts.

docs.title: Light looks wrong after a reset
docs.text:
Make sure light update packets are enabled:

reset-packets:
  send-light-updates: true

If the arena was saved with bad lighting, fix the lighting in-world and run:

/arena edit <name>

docs.title: Migration provider says "not available"
docs.text:
The plugin you are migrating from must be:

  • installed
  • enabled
  • running on the same server while you migrate

After migration is complete, you can disable or remove the old plugin.

docs.title: Migration fails for one arena
docs.text:
Try migrating one arena at a time:

/arena migrate <provider> <arena>

Confirm that the old plugin can still load or reset that arena before migrating it.

docs.title: Periodic resets feel bursty
docs.text:
Use the rotation helper for shared-area rotations:

/arena rotation <time_between_resets> <arena1> <arena2> [arena3...]

For unrelated arenas, offsets are optional. Use one only when you want an arena to start its schedule later than another arena:

/arena periodic <name> <time> <offset>

docs.title: Automatic resets need to stop temporarily
docs.text:
Pause every automatic periodic reset:

/arena pause 5m

Resume:

/arena pause off

Check status:

/arena pause status

Manual /arena reset <name> still works while automatic resets are paused.
